structured_output.hypothesis: If Darwin is right, essentially no non-volant, non-marine mammal species is verifiably native (not human-introduced) on any island whose nearest point lies more than about 483 km (300 miles) from a continent or large continental island.
structured_output.pass_criterion: After filtering and manual verification, at most 2 non-volant terrestrial mammal species (counted across all qualifying remote islands, excluding Holocene extinct taxa known only from subfossils unless dated pre-human) have a verified native status on islands >483 km from the nearest continent or large continental island. This is the stated tolerance for ambiguous cases like the Falklands and Galápagos rodents. Equivalently, more than 97% of candidate flagged records resolve to introduced, domesticated, volant, marine or misgeoreferenced.
structured_output.fail_criterion: 3 or more distinct non-volant terrestrial mammal species are verified as native (supported by pre-human fossil or genetic evidence, or an authoritative native-range source) on 3 or more separate remote islands or archipelagos >483 km from the nearest continent or large continental island. This count is made after removing human introductions.
structured_output.interpretation: "Terrestrial mammal" is read as class Mammalia excluding the order Chiroptera (bats, which Darwin explicitly treated as able to fly there) and excluding marine mammals (cetaceans, pinnipeds, sirenians). "Domesticated animals kept by natives" and human-introduced species are excluded by using the GBIF establishmentMeans field (NATIVE only) plus manual checks, because that field is often missing or wrong. "Island more than 300 miles from a continent or great continental island" is read as a great-circle distance greater than 483 km from the island's nearest coast to the nearest continental landmass or continental-shelf island. Large continental islands such as Great Britain, Borneo, Sumatra, Madagascar, New Guinea and Japan count as continents, and the distance is computed from occurrence coordinates against a coastline layer. A modern reinterpretation: the claim is tested on Holocene-native mammals, with fossil evidence of pre-human presence accepted. Madagascar is treated as a continental island, as Darwin treated it, and records on it are excluded.

dataset.name: GBIF Occurrence Data (Mammalia, georeferenced occurrence records)
dataset.why_it_fits: The GBIF occurrence search and download API (https://api.gbif.org/v1/occurrence/search) serves Mammalia records with decimalLatitude, decimalLongitude, island, islandGroup, countryCode, establishmentMeans, basisOfRecord and taxonKey/order. The plan would filter classKey=Mammalia, drop order Chiroptera, cetaceans, pinnipeds and sirenians, and keep records with establishmentMeans=NATIVE or missing. It would then compute distance to the nearest continent or large continental island from the coordinates, flag those >483 km, and verify each flagged species manually. A GBIF download generates a per-download DOI, so none is quoted for the general dataset.
